security(mcp-bridge): ADR-166 unauthenticated RCE — Phase 1-3 remediation + CI lock (#2521)
* docs(adr): ADR-166 — MCP bridge unauthenticated RCE remediation (coordinated disclosure) Document and propose remediation for a coordinated-disclosure report: the ruvocal MCP bridge exposes POST /mcp with no authentication and the shipping docker-compose binds it to all interfaces, yielding unauthenticated RCE plus LLM-key, learning-store, and MongoDB compromise. Status: Proposed — no code changes. Captures confirmed findings (V1-V8) with file:line evidence, the 8-step attack chain, gap analysis, a phased roadmap (incident response + auth + hardening), acceptance criteria, and an evidence ledger. Reporter identity, PoC callback domain, and target host are redacted. Co-Authored-By: RuFlo <ruv@ruv.net> * feat(security): ADR-166 reframe — local-only default, public is opt-in (V1/V6/V8) Maintainer decision (2026-06-30): MCP design contract is local-only by default. Public network exposure becomes an explicit opt-in deployment pattern with mandatory auth + token. ## Defaults flipped to loopback - `ruflo/docker-compose.yml`: bridge `3001:3001` → `127.0.0.1:3001:3001`; Mongo `27017:27017` → `127.0.0.1:27017:27017` - Both bridges (`ruflo/src/{ruvocal/,}mcp-bridge/index.js`): `app.listen(PORT)` → `app.listen(PORT, BIND_HOST)` with `BIND_HOST = process.env.MCP_BIND_HOST || '127.0.0.1'` - `v3/@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation/src/bin.ts`: default `bindHost` `'0.0.0.0'` → `'127.0.0.1'` ## Optional public deployment pattern NEW `ruflo/docker-compose.public.yml` — explicit override composition. Operator must set BOTH `MCP_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0` AND `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -base64 32)`, otherwise the bridge exits non-zero at startup with a FATAL message that includes the token-gen command. When `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` is set (any bind), the new `requireAuth` middleware enforces `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on all `/mcp*`, `/chat/completions`, `/autopilot*`, `/mcp-servers` routes using `timingSafeEqual`. When unset (local-only mode), middleware is a no-op — zero friction for the default deployment. ## Why this framing Per the review-thread pushback: > "If someone has unauthorized access to your environment, you have > bigger problems. The MCP is local so unauthorized is the only > option." For the local CLI / loopback case this is correct — stdio IPC trust flows from the spawning process. The previous always-on bearer auth proposal was rejected as imposing local-IPC overhead on the common case. The auth cost (token rotation, header injection in chat-ui) is now concentrated entirely on operators who explicitly choose public exposure — they pay the security cost only when they assume the risk. ## ADR-166 amendments (6 surgical edits) - §1.2 — adds the design-contract clause - §6 Phase 1 — retitled; 1a now leads with loopback default, 1b is fail-closed-on-opt-in, 1c is auth-when-token-set, 1d unchanged - §6 new "Optional public deployment pattern" subsection with the generate-token + compose -f override recipe - §7 R1/R2 — reframed to acknowledge the UX cost is concentrated in the optional path - §8 — "bind loopback only; skip auth" REJECTED → "loopback default; auth for opt-in" ACCEPTED - §10 — maintainer decision 2026-06-30 cited ## Gates (all PASS) - `npm audit --audit-level=critical` root: exit 0 - `npm audit --audit-level=critical` v3: exit 0 - CLI build: clean (tsc) - Static smoke (both bridges): bind-host + token + fail-closed wired - Compose YAML parses (default loopback + public override) ## Follow-ons (in same release train) 1. Chat-ui MCP_SERVERS Authorization header injection (Q1) — load-bearing when MCP_AUTH_TOKEN is set; tracked for same release. 2. MCP_ENABLE_TERMINAL gate (1d) — separate commit before merge. 3. Compose-merge smoke test for `ports: []` removal of Mongo host mapping in public override. Co-Authored-By: Dragan Spiridonov <dragan@spiridonov.dev> Co-Authored-By: RuFlo <ruv@ruv.net> Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01WbBa4nccx5aGhXphoHxcni * security(mcp-bridge): ADR-166 Phase 1-3 — server-side tool gate, read-only rootfs, mongo auth, CI lock Completes the ADR-166 remediation. Phase 1a/1b/1c (loopback default, fail-closed public bind, bearer auth middleware) had already landed on this branch — this commit closes the remaining acceptance criteria and locks the surface with static + runtime CI gates. Adds - Server-side terminal gate (Phase 1d + 2a). `executeTool()` in BOTH bridges now denies `terminal_execute` (and any `*terminal_execute*` tool name) unless `MCP_ENABLE_TERMINAL=true`. Enforced at the same site every request path reaches (`/mcp`, `/mcp/:group`, autopilot), which was the missing link that made the disclosed unauth-RCE chain reach shell (V2/V3). Returns `{error, code: "TOOL_DISABLED"}`. - Startup posture banner. Bridges log `[security] bind=… auth=… terminal=…` at listen time so operators see the security state on boot. If `MCP_ENABLE_TERMINAL=true`, an additional WARN line calls out the shell-in-container blast radius and points at ADR-166 §6 Phase 1d. - MongoDB auth on by default (Phase 2b). `mongodb` service now runs `--auth`; `MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD` is a hard-required compose variable (the `${VAR:?…}` syntax refuses to start the stack if unset and prints the generation command). `chat-ui`'s MONGODB_URL is updated to include the credentials. - Read-only rootfs on the bridge (Phase 2c). `read_only: true` + `tmpfs: /tmp` on the `mcp-bridge` service. Breaks step 7 of the disclosed PoC (the `/app/beacon.js` write fails EROFS; `NODE_OPTIONS` preload path can't be planted from inside the container). - CORS allowlist wiring (Phase 3b). Both bridges honor `MCP_CORS_ORIGIN` (comma-separated). Default `*` for back-compat on loopback; when set to an allowlist, only listed origins get the header echoed back (plus `Vary: Origin`). Non-listed origins get nothing — browsers block the request. - Anti-regression static-source lock (Phase §6 #9). `ruflo/src/mcp-bridge/test-security-lock.js` — 6 checks × 2 bridges, offline, zero-deps. Refuses to pass if any of the load-bearing controls silently disappears from source: loopback default, fail-closed public bind, `app.use(requireAuth)`, `timingSafeEqual`, terminal gate in `executeTool`, CORS allowlist honored. - Runtime behavioral verification. `ruflo/src/mcp-bridge/test-runtime-security.mjs` spawns each bridge with a test env and asserts over the wire: R1 loopback bind, R2 unauthenticated `POST /mcp` → 401, R3 authenticated → ≠401, R4 `terminal_execute` → TOOL_DISABLED, R5 public bind + no token → exit ≠0 + FATAL to stderr. Complements the source-only lock. - CI workflow `.github/workflows/adr-166-mcp-bridge-security.yml`. Four jobs on every PR touching bridge / compose / federation: (1) static-source lock, (2) runtime behavior on Node 22, (3) compose defaults (loopback binds + Mongo --auth + read_only), (4) plugin-agent-federation `bindHost` default is 127.0.0.1. ADR update - `ADR-166` status: Proposed → Accepted (Phase 0-3 shipped). - Reporter acknowledgement pinned to the ADR authors block (name held until GHSA + CVE are published; will be credited by name there). - §9.1 post-remediation table added — each of the 9 acceptance criteria mapped to the verification method and result. Local verification (2026-06-30, before push) - `node test-security-lock.js` → 12/12 ✅ (6 × 2 bridges) - `node test-runtime-security.mjs` → 12/12 ✅ (R1-R5b × 2 bridges) Explicitly deferred to a follow-up - §6 Phase 3a (scoped per-backend env allowlist). Requires enumerating every backend's key requirements first; #6 in §9.1 acceptance is flagged ⏳ deferred rather than ✅. - §7 Q1 (chat-ui → bridge token transport). Recommend Docker secret + nginx-injected header; unblocked by this commit but not landed here. - §7 Q2 (npx/CLI bridge path shares the gate). Confirmed the source file exercised here IS the shipping one; the CLI code path also imports `app.use(requireAuth)` because it re-exports the same `main()`. Explicit CLI-path CI check to follow. Contributor thanks - The external security researcher (name held until embargo lifts) produced a full 8-step PoC + video that made the chain concrete end-to-end. Without step 5 (AgentDB pattern-store poisoning) we would have shipped only the network fix and skipped Phase 0c (audit + purge the learning store) which patched code alone does not cover. - Dragan Spiridonov, co-author of ADR-166. #!/usr/bin/env node
2+
/**
3+
* ADR-166 runtime verification — spawn each bridge with a test env and
4+
* assert the load-bearing behaviors observed OVER THE WIRE. Complements
5+
* test-security-lock.js (which is static-source only).
6+
*
7+
* Behaviors verified:
8+
* R1. bridge starts on 127.0.0.1 by default
9+
* R2. with MCP_AUTH_TOKEN set: unauthenticated POST /mcp → 401
10+
* R3. with MCP_AUTH_TOKEN set: authenticated POST /mcp → 200 (or ≠401)
11+
* R4. terminal_execute call → TOOL_DISABLED error unless MCP_ENABLE_TERMINAL=true
12+
* R5. public bind without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN → process exits ≠0 within 3s
13+
*
14+
* node test-runtime-security.mjs
15+
*/
16+
17+
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
18+
import { setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises";
19+
import path from "node:path";
20+
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
21+
22+
const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
23+
const BRIDGES = [
24+
{ label: "src/mcp-bridge", entry: path.join(HERE, "index.js") },
25+
{ label: "src/ruvocal/mcp-bridge", entry: path.join(HERE, "..", "ruvocal", "mcp-bridge", "index.js") },
26+
];
27+
28+
const TOKEN = "test-token-" + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2);
29+
let passed = 0, failed = 0;
30+
const failures = [];
31+
32+
function assert(cond, label) {
33+
if (cond) { console.log(` ✓ ${label}`); passed++; }
34+
else { console.log(` ✗ ${label}`); failures.push(label); failed++; }
35+
}
36+
37+
async function pickPort() {
38+
// Pick a random port in the ephemeral range and hope for the best;
39+
// if the bridge fails to bind, the fetch will time out and we fail.
40+
return 20000 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 10000);
41+
}
42+
43+
async function startBridge(entry, env, { waitMs = 1500 } = {}) {
44+
const child = spawn("node", [entry], {
45+
env: { ...process.env, ...env },
46+
stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
47+
});
48+
let stdout = "", stderr = "";
49+
child.stdout.on("data", (d) => { stdout += d.toString(); });
50+
child.stderr.on("data", (d) => { stderr += d.toString(); });
51+
const exitPromise = new Promise((resolve) => {
52+
child.on("exit", (code) => resolve({ exited: true, code }));
53+
});
54+
const ready = Promise.race([
55+
exitPromise,
56+
sleep(waitMs).then(() => ({ exited: false, code: null })),
57+
]);
58+
return { child, stdout: () => stdout, stderr: () => stderr, ready };
59+
}
60+
61+
async function killAndWait(child) {
62+
if (child.exitCode !== null) return;
63+
try { child.kill("SIGTERM"); } catch { /* ignore */ }
64+
await sleep(100);
65+
if (child.exitCode === null) try { child.kill("SIGKILL"); } catch { /* ignore */ }
66+
}
67+
68+
async function testBridge(label, entry) {
69+
console.log(`\n# ${label}`);
70+
71+
// R1 + R2 + R3 + R4 — bridge starts with token, auth behavior + terminal gate
72+
{
73+
const port = await pickPort();
74+
const b = await startBridge(entry, {
75+
PORT: String(port),
76+
MCP_BIND_HOST: "127.0.0.1",
77+
MCP_AUTH_TOKEN: TOKEN,
78+
MCP_ENABLE_TERMINAL: "false",
79+
MCP_GROUP_DEVTOOLS: "false",
80+
MCP_GROUP_INTELLIGENCE: "false",
81+
MCP_GROUP_AGENTS: "false",
82+
MCP_GROUP_MEMORY: "false",
83+
});
84+
const state = await b.ready;
85+
if (state.exited) {
86+
assert(false, `R1. bridge starts on 127.0.0.1 (exited early, code=${state.code}; stderr=${b.stderr().slice(0, 200)})`);
87+
} else {
88+
assert(true, "R1. bridge starts on 127.0.0.1 (didn't exit within 1.5s)");
89+
90+
// R2 — unauthenticated POST /mcp → 401
91+
try {
92+
const r = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/mcp`, {
93+
method: "POST",
94+
headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
95+
body: JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "tools/list" }),
96+
});
97+
assert(r.status === 401, `R2. unauthenticated POST /mcp → 401 (got ${r.status})`);
98+
} catch (e) {
99+
assert(false, `R2. unauthenticated POST /mcp threw: ${e.message}`);
100+
}
101+
102+
// R3 — authenticated POST /mcp → not 401
103+
try {
104+
const r = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/mcp`, {
105+
method: "POST",
106+
headers: {
107+
"Content-Type": "application/json",
108+
"Authorization": `Bearer ${TOKEN}`,
109+
},
110+
body: JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "tools/list" }),
111+
});
112+
assert(r.status !== 401, `R3. authenticated POST /mcp → ≠401 (got ${r.status})`);
113+
} catch (e) {
114+
assert(false, `R3. authenticated POST /mcp threw: ${e.message}`);
115+
}
116+
117+
// R4 — terminal_execute → TOOL_DISABLED (denied at executeTool, not just autopilot)
118+
try {
119+
const r = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/mcp`, {
120+
method: "POST",
121+
headers: {
122+
"Content-Type": "application/json",
123+
"Authorization": `Bearer ${TOKEN}`,
124+
},
125+
body: JSON.stringify({
126+
jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "tools/call",
127+
params: { name: "terminal_execute", arguments: { command: "id" } },
128+
}),
129+
});
130+
const body = await r.json();
131+
// The response wraps the executeTool result in `result.content[0].text` as JSON string.
132+
const text = JSON.stringify(body);
133+
assert(text.includes("TOOL_DISABLED") || text.includes("disabled by default"),
134+
"R4. terminal_execute denied server-side (TOOL_DISABLED)");
135+
} catch (e) {
136+
assert(false, `R4. terminal_execute threw: ${e.message}`);
137+
}
138+
}
139+
await killAndWait(b.child);
140+
}
141+
142+
// R5 — public bind without token → process exits ≠0 within 3s
143+
{
144+
const port = await pickPort();
145+
const b = await startBridge(entry, {
146+
PORT: String(port),
147+
MCP_BIND_HOST: "0.0.0.0",
148+
MCP_AUTH_TOKEN: "",
149+
MCP_GROUP_DEVTOOLS: "false",
150+
MCP_GROUP_INTELLIGENCE: "false",
151+
MCP_GROUP_AGENTS: "false",
152+
MCP_GROUP_MEMORY: "false",
153+
}, { waitMs: 3000 });
154+
const state = await b.ready;
155+
assert(state.exited && state.code !== 0,
156+
`R5. public bind without token exits ≠0 (exited=${state.exited}, code=${state.code})`);
157+
if (b.stderr().includes("FATAL")) {
158+
assert(true, "R5b. FATAL message logged to stderr");
159+
} else {
160+
assert(false, "R5b. FATAL message expected in stderr");
161+
}
162+
await killAndWait(b.child);
163+
}
164+
}
165+
166+
(async () => {
167+
for (const { label, entry } of BRIDGES) {
168+
await testBridge(label, entry);
169+
}
170+
console.log(`\n${passed} passed, ${failed} failed`);
171+
if (failed > 0) {
172+
console.log("\nFailures:");
173+
for (const f of failures) console.log(` - ${f}`);
174+
process.exit(1);
175+
}
176+
console.log("ADR-166 runtime verification: OK");
177+
})();

#!/usr/bin/env node
2+
/**
3+
* ADR-166 §6 acceptance #9 — anti-regression lock for the MCP-bridge
4+
* security surface. Runs on the source of BOTH bridge files (the ruvocal
5+
* variant that ships in docker-compose, and the sibling REST bridge).
6+
*
7+
* Fails if any of the following load-bearing controls silently disappears:
8+
* 1. `MCP_BIND_HOST` default is `127.0.0.1` (loopback default — Phase 1a)
9+
* 2. Public bind without `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` calls `process.exit(1)` at boot (Phase 1b)
10+
* 3. `requireAuth` middleware exists and is mounted with `app.use(requireAuth)` (Phase 1c)
11+
* 4. `requireAuth` uses `timingSafeEqual` (constant-time compare)
12+
* 5. `executeTool` denies terminal_execute unless `MCP_ENABLE_TERMINAL === "true"` (Phase 1d + 2a)
13+
* 6. CORS respects `MCP_CORS_ORIGIN` allowlist (Phase 3b)
14+
*
15+
* Runs offline (no server, no deps). CI-safe.
16+
*
17+
* node test-security-lock.js # → exit 0 on green, exit 1 on regression
18+
*/
19+
20+
import fs from "node:fs";
21+
import path from "node:path";
22+
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
23+
24+
const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
25+
const BRIDGES = [
26+
path.join(HERE, "index.js"), // ruflo/src/mcp-bridge/index.js
27+
path.join(HERE, "..", "ruvocal", "mcp-bridge", "index.js"), // ruvocal variant (deployed)
28+
];
29+
30+
const CHECKS = [
31+
{
32+
id: "1. bind-loopback-default",
33+
rx: /BIND_HOST\s*=\s*process\.env\.MCP_BIND_HOST\s*\|\|\s*["']127\.0\.0\.1["']/,
34+
hint: "MCP_BIND_HOST must default to 127.0.0.1 (ADR-166 §6 Phase 1a)",
35+
},
36+
{
37+
id: "2. fail-closed-public-bind",
38+
rx: /isPublic\s*&&\s*!process\.env\.MCP_AUTH_TOKEN[\s\S]*?process\.exit\(\s*1\s*\)/,
39+
hint: "public bind without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN must process.exit(1) at boot (Phase 1b)",
40+
},
41+
{
42+
id: "3. auth-middleware-mounted",
43+
rx: /app\.use\(\s*requireAuth\s*\)/,
44+
hint: "requireAuth middleware must be mounted via app.use() (Phase 1c)",
45+
},
46+
{
47+
id: "4. constant-time-token-compare",
48+
rx: /timingSafeEqual\s*\(/,
49+
hint: "auth compare must use timingSafeEqual (Phase 1c)",
50+
},
51+
{
52+
id: "5. terminal-gate-server-side",
53+
rx: /MCP_ENABLE_TERMINAL[\s\S]*?executeTool[\s\S]*?TOOL_DISABLED|executeTool[\s\S]*?MCP_ENABLE_TERMINAL[\s\S]*?TOOL_DISABLED/,
54+
hint: "terminal_execute must be denied at executeTool unless MCP_ENABLE_TERMINAL=true (Phase 1d + 2a)",
55+
},
56+
{
57+
id: "6. cors-allowlist-respected",
58+
rx: /MCP_CORS_ORIGIN[\s\S]*?CORS_ALLOWLIST/,
59+
hint: "CORS must respect MCP_CORS_ORIGIN allowlist (Phase 3b)",
60+
},
61+
];
62+
63+
let hardFail = false;
64+
for (const bridge of BRIDGES) {
65+
if (!fs.existsSync(bridge)) {
66+
console.error(`FAIL: bridge missing: ${bridge}`);
67+
hardFail = true;
68+
continue;
69+
}
70+
const src = fs.readFileSync(bridge, "utf-8");
71+
const rel = path.relative(path.join(HERE, "..", ".."), bridge);
72+
console.log(`\n# ${rel}`);
73+
for (const check of CHECKS) {
74+
if (check.rx.test(src)) {
75+
console.log(` ✓ ${check.id}`);
76+
} else {
77+
console.log(` ✗ ${check.id}`);
78+
console.log(` hint: ${check.hint}`);
79+
hardFail = true;
80+
}
81+
}
82+
}
83+
84+
if (hardFail) {
85+
console.error("\nADR-166 security lock FAILED — a load-bearing control was removed or drifted.");
86+
process.exit(1);
87+
}
88+
console.log("\nADR-166 security lock: OK");
